cs.t: I’m still rocking my OG first gen MX Master today, 11+ years and counting of daily backpack tossing, having survived 3 MacBooks and at least 7 chargers. My only secret? I bought a $10 padded case for it on Amazon the very first day I had the mouse, and zip it in there every time before it goes in my backpack. Everything works as new, the only thing that broke is the plastic covering the gesture button.

cs.t: I have been using the original MX Master for about 4 years now and the mouse has been a dream. Absolutely great build quality and perfect ergonomics (for a right handed person).

cs.t: Counterpoint/anecdata, I've had 3 MX Master mice and 2 died in under a year and the third lasted about 2 weeks past the 2 year warranty expiration. And this was babying them, no mistreatment. I gave up and switched to a clone (Rapoo MT760) that I actually like more.

cs.t: I've used an MX Master 2S for two years now and this is the first time I've thought about it for more than five seconds. Now that I'm considering it, though, this is easily the nicest scroll wheel I've ever used.

cs.t: I bought a Logitech trackball (the MX5something), and the switches stopped working a year in. Amazon refunded me, so I bought an MX Master 3S. The switches for that  also  stopped working a year in. I complained to the merchant and Logitech, and luckily they sent me a new mouse each. I also bought some replacement switches and repaired the lot, so now I have four mouses/trackballs. Still, they should make better mouses.
cs.th: Building the mouse Logitech won't make

cs.t: I had two mouses get that problem about a year in. One was the MX Master 3S, a 100 € mouse. For that price point, it's entirely unacceptable for the mouse to only last a year. Good thing it had a two year warranty, but it's such a hassle to be without a mouse for weeks.

cs.t:
Good to see open source alternatives to the awful Logitech software. I only realized how bad the Logitech software is after switching from a G502 with on-board memory to an MX Master mouse that does not have on-board memory and needs to have the app constantly running in the background to use the gestures. 
Personally I've been using BetterMouse on macOS with my MX Master, although it's not open source.
cs.th: OpenLogi

cs.t: I've been a trackpad proponent for years, but with Steermouse I've been able to dial in my MX Master so perfectly that I find myself missing it when I travel. What really took it to the next level for me were adding chord mappings. For example I can hold right mouse button + scroll the thumb wheel to adjust volume. So convenient!
cs.th: OpenLogi

cs.t: For pro gaming perhaps the difference would make the slightest difference. For casuals, let alone office workers, the difference is 0 (writing this with a mx master 4 next to me). Saying this as someone who has tried dozens of mice in my life. Last corded-one, bought for my son yesterday (razer cobra minecraft edition). I don't think I'd be able to tell the difference between wired and wireless in a blind test.
cs.th: OpenLogi

cs.t: There's also SteerMouse, which I use to configure my MX Master settings. One of the benefits is it's not something that needs to run continuously in your menu bar: you can set options and close it. In the end, it's just a basic peripheral...  https://plentycom.jp/en/steermouse/
cs.th: OpenLogi

cs.t: I use the Master MX 3s specifically because of the "gestures" button, it was mandatory for me to replace using the trackpad. It's basically a thumb button you can press and combine with a mouse gesture to do the same thing as finger gestures on the trackpad. I mainly use the gestures left/right (to switch between full screen apps/main dektop) and up (mission control) but it's all configurable. It also has an horizontal scroll wheel that's very useful when using Excel or DB viewers.
cs.th: OpenLogi

cs.t: That was a frustrating fix. The MX Master has a "gesture" button under the rubber where your thumb rests. I don't believe I ever used it intentionally. But because it is a gesture button, when it fails the mouse no longer responds as it always thinks it is gesturing. Pull the wire and it is fine, but diagnosing it is rough.
cs.th: Repair Cafe – Fix Your Broken Items

cs.t: I've done this fix on at least 3 MX Masters, just going in through the rubber on the side to remove the switch, since disassembly through unscrewing everything is more work. Needing to replace the feet every time you open the mouse is pretty frustrating. This applies to the MX Master 1 & 2.
cs.th: Repair Cafe – Fix Your Broken Items

cs.t:
I'm stuck in the same relationship with them:
MX Master 3s/4 is my perfect productivity mouse. Problem? The rubber coating gradually disintegrates and accumulates dirt.
ERGO K860 is my perfect keyboard. Problem? The plastic ABS surface of the keys wears and smooths in just a few months. The first set of AAA batteries have a far longer life! If only they didn't cheap out on the materials and plastic quality.
cs.th: I love my Bluetooth keyboard

cs.t: I have a Iiyama with build in hub, at first it seemed ideal, just plug everything into the monitor. But my mouse glitches when used through the hub (MX Master 3S), the internet cable is only available to the active computer (so no tasks requiring internet can run on the other computer). All in all, I just use the USB-C to HDMI switch functionality and couple the computers to keyboard/mouse via bluetooth, plus I bought a switch for the ethernet. It's a shame it's so suboptimal. Another minor annoyance is that when I turn off one computer and want to switch to the other, the display turns off, taking about 5-10 sec to do so. Then I manually turn it back on and it's ready in another 3 sec. So I do this thing where I hover about the turn-off button, hit it and immediately switch so the monitor won't turn off. It's hard to make convenient tech it seems.
cs.th: Two computers, one monitor, zero fiddling – Alex Plescan

cs.t: Huh. Haven't experienced that myself, having used a Master MX for several years (now in use by my wife), a VX Revolution for a few years before that (now my son's backpack mouse), and a Master MX Vertical most recently. My son has gone through several other Logi mice as his primary mice, too, but they've died of either worn out switches or feet (he's an avid gamer). Not trying to invalidate your experience -- I've see with my own eyes a similar thing happen with rubberized coatings on laptops & keyboard wrist rests (other's not my own). Just putting it out there that it's by no means the universal experience.

cs.t: I loved my Performance MX. I finally had to replace it at work (software wouldn't install after migrating to Windows 11) and the MX Master 3 I got seems much ergonomically worse to me. I also am not a fan of the thumb wheel replacing buttons. Only thing I won't complain about is that the resolution is better. From testing my coworkers' mouses (older Masters) I'm pretty sure they have each been a step downhill from my perspective. My sister in law gave me her G700S to fix the main button microswitches, and she convinced me that it's the apotheosis of the design - it's what should have replaced the Performance MX. No soft-touch plastic, extra buttons, and the higher resolution sensor. I'll probably have to get one off eBay. Edit: also all of the Masters have non-user-replaceable batteries.
cs.th: The struggle of resizing windows on macOS Tahoe

cs.t: I also use the magic trackpad. I even tried the renowned logitech mx master 4 but returned it the next day, heavy and straining for the wrist. And all of the extra buttons and actions on that mouse don't make much sense when the trackpad has gestures.
